mainTopic: The טומאה of the פרים ושעירים הנשרפים, the פרה and the שעיר המשתלח: when carriers' בגדים become טמא, when the animals make food and drink טמא, and whether they need הכשר.
overview: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's question about an offering that is partly out of the עזרה: do we follow the limb, or the whole animal? It ends in תיקו, and so does רבה בר רב הונא's version about three of five carriers being outside. רבי אלעזר then asks about an offering that went out and came back. רבי אבא בר ממל tries to answer from a משנה about carriers on poles. רבינא rejects that proof, because the פסוק says 'afterward he may come into the camp', so a carrier must be outside to become טמא. A ברייתא follows in which רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue whether the שעיר המשתלח makes food and drink טמא. The גמרא explains both views through the rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל about הכשר. רבי אלעזר then rules that the burned bulls and goats, while still inside the עזרה, need הכשר like ordinary food. Finally, a question is raised about the size of נבלת עוף טהור needed to make food טמא according to רבי מאיר. Its answer begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: Follow the limb or follow the whole animal?
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי אלעזר's question: when part of the animal is outside, do we judge by the limb that is mostly out, or by the animal, which is not mostly out?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we judge it by most of the limb, and most of the limb has gone out? Or do we judge it by the animal as a whole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that started before this section. It lays out the two sides: follow the limb, or follow the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of one limb has left the עזרה, but the animal as a whole has not mostly left. If we look at the limb, it counts as 'out' and בגדים become טמא. If we look at the whole animal, it is still 'in', and they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: we 'throw it' after; we decide its status by

phrases.english: Do we decide it by the majority of the limb,
and that has gone out;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בָּתַר בְּהֵמָה שָׁדֵינַן לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps we decide it by the animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר רוֹב אֵבֶר שָׁדֵינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's question from before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a partly-out offering count as 'out' because most of a limb is out, or as 'in' because most of the animal is not out?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבי אלעזר's question unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The question stays open; it is not decided for either side.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether we follow the limb or the whole animal is left unresolved.

steps.title: The same question, asked about the carriers
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא teaches the question about people: five carry the offering, three are out and two are in. Do we follow most of the carriers or the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא teaches it about people. Five people are handling the offering. Three went out and two stayed inside. What is the law? Do we follow most of the handlers, or do we follow the animal?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second version of the same question. Here the 'majority' is about the people carrying, not about a limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the carriers (three of five) are already outside the עזרה, but most of the animal has not left yet. So the question is which one decides: where most of the carriers are, or where the animal is.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּגַבְרֵי,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna teaches it with regard to people:
where five people are handling it,

phrases.aramaic: וּנְפַקוּ תְּלָתָא וּפָשׁוּ לְהוּ תְּרֵי – מַאי?
phrases.english: and three went out and two remained, what is the law?
Do we follow the majority of the handlers,
or do we follow the animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּגַבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the question from step 1, about carriers instead of a limb.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do we follow the majority of carriers who are out, or the animal, which is mostly still in?

steps.title: This version also stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא's version also ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version of the question is also left without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither version gets settled. We do not know whether the carriers or the animal decide the matter.
steps.whatToRemember: Both partial-exit questions (most of a limb out, or most of the carriers out) end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether we follow the carriers or the animal is left unresolved.

steps.title: An offering that went out and came back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks: if the פרים ושעירים הנשרפים left the עזרה and came back in, do they still make the carriers' בגדים טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: bulls and goats that are burned, which went out and came back, what is the law? Do we say that once they went out, they became טמא? Or perhaps, once they came back, they came back?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר opens a brand-new question about an offering that left the עזרה and then returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says leaving the עזרה changes the offering for good, so it stays able to make בגדים טמא even back inside. The other side says that coming back puts it back where it was, so carrying it inside would not make בגדים טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: the bulls and goats that are burned outside the camp

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
Bulls and goats that are burned
that went out and came back, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: do the carriers' clothes become טמא when they carry it inside again?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקִי לְהוּ – אִיטַּמּוֹ לְהוּ;
phrases.english: Do we say: once they went out, they became impure;
or perhaps, once they came back, they came back?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question by the same אמורא after the earlier ones ended in תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does going out permanently make the offering able to make בגדים טמא, or does returning undo that?

steps.title: A משנה about carriers on poles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל brings a משנה: carriers who have passed outside the עזרה wall make their בגדים טמא, but those behind them who are still inside do not, until they go out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: Come and hear. They would carry them on poles. The front carriers went out beyond the wall of the עזרה and the back carriers did not go out. The front ones, who went out beyond the wall of the עזרה, make their בגדים טמא. The back ones do not make their בגדים טמא until they go out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל quotes a משנה to try to answer רבי אלעזר's question. Here he only lays out the source; the reasoning comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the back carriers are still inside, even though the offering on the poles has already started going out. Their בגדים are not טמא until they themselves go out.

keyTerms.meaning: the wall of the Temple courtyard

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said: Come and hear:
They would carry them on poles;
if the first ones went out beyond the wall of the courtyard
phrases.notes: 'The first ones' are the carriers at the front of the poles.

phrases.english: and the last ones did not go out,
the first ones, who went out beyond the wall of the courtyard,
make their garments impure,
and the last ones do not make their garments impure
until they go out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer רבי אלעזר's question from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's question about an offering that went out and came back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about priests carrying the offering on poles, front ones out and back ones in.

steps.title: Why the משנה answers the question
steps.stepSummary: If the offering became טמא for good as soon as it went out, even the carriers still inside should have טמא בגדים. They don't, so going out does not permanently change the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that once they go out they become טמא, then these carriers who are still inside should become טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל explains how the משנה proves his point. He argues from the case of the back carriers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering on the poles has already gone out. If that alone made it permanently able to make בגדים טמא, the back carriers would be טמא even while standing inside. The משנה says they are not, so it seems that being inside means no טומאה. That would mean an offering brought back inside does not make בגדים טמא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא בר ממל uses the back carriers, who are inside and not טמא, to argue that only being outside causes the טומאה. So an offering that came back inside should not make בגדים טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: The back carriers are not טמא even though the offering itself has already started leaving. That is the whole basis of the proof.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that once they go out they become impure,
these who are inside should become impure!
phrases.notes: Some versions have לִיטָּמֵא (in round brackets); the corrected wording is לִיטַּמּוֹ (in square brackets), 'they should become impure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקִי לְהוּ אִיטַּמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה from step 6 answers the question in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The side of the question that says returning undoes the offering's going out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The back carriers in the משנה, who stay טהור while inside even though the offering has already left.

steps.title: רבינא rejects the proof from the carriers still inside
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the carriers still inside the עזרה stay טהור for a different reason. The פסוק requires that they 'come into the camp' afterward, and they never left it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Do you really think this is a proof? I need the words 'and afterward he may come into the camp', and that is not the case here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down the proof from step 7. He says the carriers still inside are טהור for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the inside carriers are טהור because leaving the עזרה did not permanently change the offering. רבינא says no. The פסוק only applies this טומאה to someone who will later 'come into the camp', so a person must first be outside. That explains the inside carriers without proving anything about an offering that went out and came back.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a way of rejecting an idea)
camp. Here it is the area the carrier must later come back into
it is not there / not present

phrases.english: Ravina said: And can you really think so?!
But I need "and afterward he may come into the camp"
and that is missing here!
phrases.notes: The carriers still inside never went out, so they can't 'come back in'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: וְתִסְבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about carriers inside versus outside
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inside carriers are טהור because the פסוק requires them to be outside the camp, not because of the offering's status

steps.title: So what was רבי אלעזר asking?
steps.stepSummary: If carriers can only become טמא once they are outside, the גמרא asks what case רבי אלעזר's question could be about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how did רבי אלעזר ask his question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רבי אלעזר had in mind, now that רבינא has changed the picture. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the offering comes back in, anyone carrying it is standing inside. By רבינא's rule, such a person could never become טמא anyway. So רבי אלעזר's question seems to have no case left, and the גמרא needs to find one.

keyTerms.meaning: how did he ask it? (what case was he asking about?)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֵיכִי בָּעֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rather, how did Rabbi Elazar ask his question?
phrases.notes: This goes back to his question in step 5, about the offering that went out and came back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֵיכִי בָּעֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבינא's rule and asks how רבי אלעזר's question still makes sense
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case רבי אלעזר's question is about

steps.title: The case: carrying it out with poles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asked about people standing outside who take the animal out with poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where they hold it with poles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is people standing outside the עזרה who hold the offering with poles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These carriers are already outside, so the rule of 'afterward he may come into the camp' can apply to them. Now the real question is clear. Does an offering that went out and came back in still make these outside carriers' בגדים טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: for example / such as a case where

phrases.english: For example, where they hold it with poles.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן דִּנְקִיטִי לַהּ בְּבָקוּלְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about carriers outside the עזרה who take the offering out with poles
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: a carrier becomes טמא only once he is outside, because the פסוק says 'afterward he may come into the camp'. So רבי אלעזר's question is about outside carriers using poles.

steps.title: ברייתא: who becomes impure from the bulls, heifer and scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the people who send, burn or take out these animals make their בגדים טמא. The animals themselves don't make בגדים טמא. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue whether the שעיר המשתלח makes food and drink טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: For the bulls, the פרה and the שעיר המשתלח, the one who sends, the one who burns them and the one who takes them out make their בגדים impure. The animals themselves do not make בגדים impure, but they do make food and drink impure. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say: the פרה and the bulls make food and drink impure, but the שעיר המשתלח does not, since it is alive, and a living thing does not make food and drink impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the טומאה of the burned פרים, the פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח. It includes an argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the people who handle these animals make their בגדים טמא, and the animals themselves don't. They argue about one thing: does the living שעיר המשתלח make אוכלין ומשקין טמא? רבי מאיר says yes. חכמים say no, because a living animal cannot pass on this טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the goat sent away on יום כיפור

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פָּרִים וּפָרָה וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: bulls, and the heifer, and the scapegoat —
the one who sends, the one who burns them, and the one who takes them out make garments impure;
phrases.notes: Each person matches one animal. Someone sends the goat away, and someone burns the bulls and the heifer.

phrases.english: but the animals themselves do not make garments impure,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְטַמְּאִין אֳוכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין. דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: but they do make food and drink impure. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: פָּרָה וּפָרִים מְטַמְּאִין אֳוכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: the heifer and the bulls make food and drink impure,
the scapegoat does not make things impure,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַי, וְהַחַי אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֳוכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין.
phrases.english: since it is alive, and a living thing does not make food and drink impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פָּרִים וּפָרָה וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a ברייתא about the טומאה of animals sent out of the עזרה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handlers make their בגדים טמא, and the animals do not. רבי מאיר says all three make אוכלין ומשקין טמא. חכמים exclude the living שעיר המשתלח.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of טומאה here. Making בגדים טמא applies to the people handling the animals. Making food and drink טמא is about the animals themselves.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's view fits a teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי מאיר's view makes sense based on a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל, which begins with the words 'upon any sowing seed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי מאיר, it is like what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught. For the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "Upon any sowing seed"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining where רבי מאיר's view comes from by quoting a teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל. The teaching continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בשלמא' signals that רבי מאיר's view is easy to explain. It also hints that the גמרא will soon ask what the source is for חכמים. The proof is built on a פסוק about seeds, and the full reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: granted / it makes sense (one view is fine, a question on the other view usually follows)
a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל;
phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir, it is like what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught;

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״עַל כׇּל זֶרַע זֵרוּעַ״ –
phrases.english: for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: "Upon any sowing seed" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:37. The teaching keeps going in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins finding the source for רבי מאיר's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that the animals, even the living שעיר, make אוכלין ומשקין טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל on the פסוק 'על כל זרע זרוע' (ויקרא 11:37)

steps.title: Only things that can never become severely impure need to be made ready
steps.stepSummary: The teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל compares everything to seeds. Like seeds, anything that can never carry severe טומאה needs הכשר. Something that can carry severe טומאה, like נבלת עוף טהור, does not need הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeds can never carry severe impurity, and they need to be made ready before they can become impure. So too, anything that can never carry severe impurity needs to be made ready. That leaves out the carcass of a kosher bird: it can carry severe impurity, so it does not need to be made ready.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the teaching it started in the last step. That teaching is the proof for רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is: only things that can never carry severe טומאה need הכשר. The burned bulls, the פרה and the שעיר המשתלח all make people טמא, which is severe טומאה. So by this rule they make food טמא without any הכשר, which is exactly what רבי מאיר says.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeds; the example the פסוק uses for food
Making food ready to become טמא, normally by getting it wet
Severe impurity, the kind that can make a person טמא
The carcass of a kosher bird, which makes a person טמא when he swallows it

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for רבי מאיר's view. It is also the rule the חכמים will need to explain in the next step.

phrases.english: Just as seeds,
phrases.notes: This continues the פסוק from the last step, 'upon any sowing seed' (ויקרא 11:37).

phrases.english: which will never become impure with a severe impurity,
need to be made ready;
so too, anything that will never
become impure with a severe impurity
needs to be made ready.
This leaves out the carcass of a kosher bird,
which does become impure with a severe impurity,
and so it does not need to be made ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה זְרָעִים שֶׁאֵין סוֹפָן לְיטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that step 12 began quoting.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that these animals make food and drink טמא on their own
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל on 'upon any sowing seed', which says only things that can never carry severe טומאה need הכשר

steps.title: How can the חכמים split the שעיר המשתלח from the bulls?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are caught in a squeeze. If they accept the teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל, the שעיר המשתלח should also make food טמא. If they reject it, there is no source that the פרה and the bulls make food טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how does this work for the חכמים? If they accept the teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל, then even the שעיר המשתלח should make food impure! If they don't accept it, how do we know that even the פרה and the bulls make food impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view of the חכמים. They say the bulls and the פרה make food טמא, but the שעיר המשתלח does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל treats all of these animals the same way. Every one of them makes people טמא. So the חכמים seem to have no basis for treating the שעיר המשתלח differently from the bulls and the פרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים who argue with רבי מאיר
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
The פרה אדומה, the red heifer
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis:
if they hold
the teaching of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
then even the scapegoat should make food impure!
And if they don't hold it,
then for even the heifer and the bulls, how do we know they make food impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן אִי אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving רבי מאיר's view, the גמרא turns to the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the חכמים in the ברייתא from step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a two-sided trap. Accepting the rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל includes the שעיר המשתלח too. Rejecting the rule leaves the bulls and the פרה with no source.

steps.title: רב דימי: according to the חכמים, these animals first need to become impure from something else
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings the answer from ארץ ישראל. The חכמים hold that the bulls and the פרה make food טמא only after they themselves have become טמא from another source. The live שעיר המשתלח cannot become טמא that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: In the West they say that these animals need to be made ready by becoming impure from somewhere else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not accept the rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל here. They hold that the bulls and the פרה must first pick up טומאה from some other source, and only then do they make food טמא. A living animal like the שעיר המשתלח cannot pick up טומאה, so it never makes food טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the West'; this means ארץ ישראל
From another place, here meaning from another source of טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds that all of these animals make food טמא on their own, based on the teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. The חכמים hold that they must first become טמא from something else. So the living שעיר המשתלח does not make food טמא according to them.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
In the West they say:
They need to be made ready by impurity
from somewhere else.
phrases.notes: He means they first have to touch some other source of טומאה before they can make food טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge against the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks the second side of the trap and gives a different source of טומאה for the bulls and the פרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the חכמים needed the rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל to explain why the bulls and the פרה make food טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the חכמים, the bulls and the פרה make food טמא only after they pick up טומאה from another source. The living שעיר המשתלח cannot pick up טומאה, so it does not make food טמא.

steps.title: Do the burned bulls and goats make food impure while still inside the עזרה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether the burned bulls and goats already make food and drink טמא while still inside the עזרה. The question is whether 'not yet taken out' counts like 'still missing a needed action'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: The bulls and goats that are burned, do they make food and drink impure inside the עזרה, just like they do outside? Is something that has not yet been taken out treated like something still missing an action, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question from רבי אלעזר. Earlier he asked about the people carrying the animals; now he asks about food and drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the עזרה, these animals make people טמא. That is why, by the rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל, they make food טמא without הכשר. Inside, they have not yet been taken out and do not yet make people טמא. The question is whether that missing step makes them like something not yet finished, which would still need הכשר, or whether they already count as finished.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question he did not know the answer to
Inside the עזרה just like outside

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different question from רבי אלעזר's earlier one in step 5, which steps 9 and 10 clarified. That one was about the people carrying the animal; this one is about food and drink touching the animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
The bulls and goats that are burned,
what is the law, do they make food and drink impure
inside, just like outside?
Is something still missing being taken out
treated like something still missing an action,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר פָּרִים וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that these animals make food טמא, and asks whether that rule already applies before they leave the עזרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether being 'not yet taken out' counts as still missing a needed action, so that inside the עזרה the animals would not yet make food and drink טמא.

steps.title: Not yet taken out counts like missing an action
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers his own question. Bulls and goats not yet taken out of the עזרה count like something still missing an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked the question, he answered it himself: something that has not yet been taken out is treated like something that is still missing a needed action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question he asked in the previous step. While the burned bulls and goats are still inside the עזרה, they do not make food and drink טמא unless they first get הכשר, just like ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that something still missing a needed action is not yet in its final state. רבי אלעזר now says that 'not yet taken out' belongs in that same group. So inside the עזרה the bulls and goats are like ordinary food: they need הכשר before they can make food and drink טמא. Only once they leave do they make food טמא without הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Still missing the act of being taken out

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, burned bulls and goats inside the עזרה do not make food and drink טמא without הכשר. 'Not yet taken out' counts like 'still missing an action'.

phrases.english: After he asked it
he then resolved it:
Something missing being taken out
is like something missing an action.
phrases.notes: So while they are still inside the עזרה, they need הכשר like ordinary food before they can make food and drink טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דְּבַעְיַאּ הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי אלעזר asked in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מחוסר יציאה כמחוסר מעשה דמי: before they are taken out, the bulls and goats do not make food and drink טמא without הכשר.

steps.title: Does a kosher bird carcass make food impure at an olive's size?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר שמואל asks רבי חייא בר אבא a question. According to רבי מאיר, does נבלת עוף טהור make food טמא with only a כזית?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר שמואל asked רבי חייא בר אבא: according to רבי מאיר, does נבלת עוף טהור make things impure with just a כזית?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי מאיר holds that נבלת עוף טהור makes food טמא even without הכשר, so the question is: what is the minimum size it needs to do that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal טמא food needs to be the size of an egg to pass טומאה to other food. But נבלת עוף טהור makes a person טמא when he swallows just a כזית. So we ask which size counts when it makes food טמא: the food size or the smaller person size.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a kosher bird that was not slaughtered properly
An olive's size, a smaller amount than an egg's size

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Shmuel asked
of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
The carcass of a kosher bird, according to Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר is the one who said it makes food טמא even without הכשר (Steps 12–13).

phrases.english: what is the law: does it make impure with an olive's size?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי מאיר's view about נבלת עוף טהור and opens a new question about its minimum size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי מאיר, does נבלת עוף טהור make food טמא with a כזית, or only with the usual egg's size?

steps.title: Narrowing the question to meat held in the hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets aside two easy cases, meat on the ground and meat in the mouth. The real question is about meat held in the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is lying on the ground, don't ask. If he holds it in his mouth, don't ask. Ask only when he holds it in his hand: is something not yet brought close treated like something missing an action, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the question sharper. It shows which case is actually in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat lying on the ground is clearly just ordinary food and needs an egg's size. Meat already in the mouth is about to be swallowed, so a כזית surely works. Meat in the hand is in between: does 'not yet brought close' count like 'missing an action', so that it is still treated as regular food?

keyTerms.meaning: Do not ask about this case, because its answer is clear
Not yet brought close (to the mouth to be swallowed)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same idea as Step 17's 'missing an action', applied to a new case. In Step 17 the question was being taken out of the עזרה. Here it is being brought close to the mouth.

phrases.english: Where it is lying on the ground –
do not ask;
phrases.notes: On the ground, it is clearly just ordinary food, so it needs an egg's size.

phrases.english: where he holds it in his mouth –
do not ask;
when you should ask –
is where he holds it in his hand:
Something missing being brought close
is it like something missing an action, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 18 to the one case that is actually in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does meat held in the hand, not yet brought close to the mouth, count as 'missing an action', so that it needs an egg's size?

steps.title: The asker begins to answer his own question
steps.stepSummary: After asking the question, the one who asked turns to answer it himself. The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked the question, he answered it himself:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The one who asked is about to give his own answer, and the answer itself comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses the same phrase it used in Step 17. That phrase tells us the asker will settle the question himself, without anyone else stepping in.

phrases.english: After he asked it
he then resolved it:

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דְּבַעְיַאּ הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the answer to the question in Steps 18–19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer itself comes right after this line; here the asker only begins to resolve it.
